​לרבים היה נדמה כי הטרור באיו"ש נגמר - אך זו מציאות מתעתעת לחלוטין. הטרור אף פעם לא נגמר, הוא דעך זמנית עד להתפרצותו מחדש. טיפול נקודתי לאחר הפיגוע לא יוביל לשום שינוי. התגובה צריכה להיות כוללת: כנגד האוכלוסייה הערבית באיו"ש ותושבי הכפרים מהם יצאו המחבלים, וכנגד משטרי הטרור בעזה וברמאללה שמשלחים, מממנים, מחנכים ומסיתים לטרור - והופכים אותו לכלי אפקטיבי אף יותר מרקטות או טילים בליסטיים מאיראן.

item.title: [amitseg] The head of the Israel Security Agency (Shin Bet), David Zini, held a situational assessment at the scene of the attack
item.description:
Open
The head of the Israel Security Agency (Shin Bet), David Zini, held a situational assessment at the scene of the attack with Shin Bet commanders from the Samaria district and IDF commanders in the sector. During the assessment, instructions were issued to intensify Shin Bet intelligence-gathering and counterterrorism operations in villages in the area, as well as additional offensive actions against terrorist infrastructure in the sector.

Shin Bet Director David Zini said:

"This morning's attack was severe and painful, and tragically claimed a heavy toll in lives. On my behalf and on behalf of all the men and women of the Shin Bet, I extend my condolences to the families and wish the injured a speedy recovery.

We are working tirelessly, shoulder to shoulder with the regional command and division commanders, and with the commanders and soldiers of the IDF, to thwart terrorism in the area.

We are conducting continuous situational assessments with the IDF, investigating the attack, and taking the necessary operational measures, which we will expand and deepen as operational needs require.

In recent months, we have foiled dozens of attacks, almost every night. This time, we were unable to prevent it in advance. We will continue to act and will reach everyone who carried out the attack or is planning to harm Israeli civilians.

I call on the public not to take the law into their own hands and to place their trust in the IDF and the Israel Security Agency, whose mission and responsibility this is."

item.title: [englishabuali] The following was posted today on Facebook by KKL-JNF Chairman and Israel's Avoda (Labor) Party member Eyal Ostrinsky:
item.description:
Open
The following was posted today on Facebook by KKL-JNF Chairman and Israel's Avoda (Labor) Party member Eyal Ostrinsky:

Strengthening Security-Oriented Settlement and Social Fulfillment in the Jordan Valley

Last Wednesday, we held a highly significant working tour of the Jordan Valley together with members of the MAFK Committee, its chairman Yehoshua Sherman, Settlement Division head Yishai Merling, the division’s director-general Hoshaya Harari and their team, Jordan Valley Division Commander Brig. Gen. Oren Simcha, and the commander of the Jordan Valley Brigade.

In the Gaon Hayarden area, east of the security barrier, we met pioneering settlers who established agricultural farms as security outposts, with the encouragement of the IDF, and as a critical component of efforts to prevent smuggling and infiltration along Israel’s eastern border with Jordan.

We also met representatives of Hashomer HaChadash and other organizations leading the establishment of new sites on the ground, including student villages, pre-military academies, Nahal groups, and more. 

We heard about their challenges and needs, and discussed how KKL-JNF could assist them.

We also held a moving meeting with Bezalel Wiberman, founder of “A Home in the Valley,” who leads efforts to rescue at-risk youth and help them return to meaningful service in the IDF and productive participation in Israeli society. The organization also operates a pre-military academy that brings 30 young people each year to spend a meaningful year in the Jordan Valley before enlisting in the IDF.

We were deeply moved to hear the stories of participants who had been on the verge of complete collapse, but who, thanks to Bezalel and his work, went on to serve—or are currently serving—in some of the IDF’s most elite units, or found meaning through other forms of significant contribution to society.

Nothing could be more important or moving.
We concluded with an important discussion with Brig. Gen. Oren Simcha, the division commander and, coincidentally, the brother of my dear colleague Lior Simcha, secretary-general of the Kibbutz Movement. He presented the IDF’s security concept for the region, within which settlement is defined as a critical component. This includes security outposts east of the barrier, the expansion and reinforcement of existing Jordan Valley communities, and the establishment of new settlement points along the entire border, from the Arava to the eastern shore of the Sea of Galilee.

The division commander asked KKL-JNF, alongside the Settlement Division, to become involved in this Zionist effort of major security importance. We will examine the matter in the coming period and make decisions accordingly and swiftly, in order to help settlement throughout the eastern border region—and particularly in the Jordan Valley—grow and expand, while contributing to Israel’s security.

Strengthening the eastern border is another national mission before us. For me, strengthening the Jordan Valley as part of this effort enjoys broad national consensus. 

At KKL-JNF, in keeping with the tradition of this term, we will be wherever we are needed and contribute everything we can.

At the same time, organizations such as A Home in the Valley, which carry out life-saving social work with struggling and disconnected youth—especially those at the very edge of the spectrum—while operating within a framework of national fulfillment in the Jordan Valley, are critical to our social resilience. This is certainly something we will seek to strengthen in the coming period, beginning this year and with even greater intensity in the years ahead.

I am proud of Bezalel, whom I met for the first time, and of his Zionist and social work.

We will stand alongside him to help save more and more young people and give them genuine purpose and an opportunity to fulfill their potential.

Shabbat shalom to everyone.
